# secopsctl rules

Your CUSTOM detections: author, test, deploy, and inspect (Google-managed rules are under `curated`)

## rules alerts

Read-only: search alerts a rule generated (raw, rule-dependent shape)

```text
secopsctl rules alerts <rule-id> [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--hours` | int | 24 | look-back window in hours |

## rules counts

Read-only: rule count and quota statistics for the instance

```text
secopsctl rules counts
```

## rules detections

Read-only: list detections a rule produced in a time window

```text
secopsctl rules detections <rule> [flags]
```

```text
List the detections a rule produced over the last --hours.
<rule> is a rule id, display name, or slug as shown by `rules list`.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--hours` | int | 24 | look-back window in hours |
| `--limit` | int | 100 | max detections (page size) |
| `--state` | string | - | filter by alert state (e.g. ALERTING) |

## rules duplicate

MUTATING (guarded): clone a rule's YARA-L under a new name (created disabled)

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl rules duplicate <rule> [--name NEW] [flags]
```

```text
Copy an existing rule's YARA-L into a new rule with a new name token — the
console's Duplicate Rule. The clone is created DISABLED and non-alerting (a
fresh rule has no deployment); deploy it with `rules promote`/`push rules-deploy`
when ready. <rule> is an id, display name, or slug. --name sets the new rule's
name (default: the source name + "_copy"). Re-run `pull rules` to mirror the
clone. Guarded: dry-run by default, --yes to apply.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--name` | string | - | name for the clone (default: source name + "_copy") |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## rules events

Read-only: the UDM events behind one detection (the evidence pivot)

```text
secopsctl rules events <rule> <detection-id> [flags]
```

```text
Fetch the events a detection matched — the evidence an analyst inspects
before a verdict, without hand-writing a `query udm`. <rule> is a rule id,
display name, or slug; <detection-id> comes from `rules detections`.
Human output summarizes samples per event variable; --json is the full payload.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--max` | int | 0 | max events over all event variables (0 = server default) |

## rules get

Read-only: show a rule's current state + YARA-L (is it running, and what it says)

```text
secopsctl rules get <rule> [flags]
```

```text
Fetch the latest version of a rule and show whether it is running (enabled/
alerting/archived, compile + execution state, severity, MITRE) followed by its
YARA-L. <rule> is an id, display name, or slug. --text prints just the YARA-L
(raw, for piping into `rules promote` or a diff); --json emits the full rule +
deployment.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--text` | bool | false | print only the YARA-L text (raw, pipe-friendly) |

## rules health

Read-only: per-rule health roll-up (compile / execution / silence) across all rules

```text
secopsctl rules health [flags]
```

```text
One read that classifies every rule by health and lists the worst first:
  failing  — does not compile
  erroring — deployment execution is limited/paused
  silent   — enabled + alerting but produced no detections in the window
  healthy  — everything else
Composes the rule list, deployments, and detection trends over the last
--hours. --only narrows to one bucket.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--format` | string | - | output: table \| json \| csv (default table; overrides the global --output/--json) |
| `--hours` | int | 168 | detection-trend look-back window in hours (default 7d) |
| `--only` | string | - | show only one bucket: failing \| erroring \| silent \| healthy |
| `--out` | string | - | write to a file instead of stdout |


## rules promote

MUTATING (guarded): create a new rule from a file and deploy it in one step

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl rules promote <file.yaral> [flags]
```

```text
Validate a YARA-L file, create the live rule, and deploy it to the requested
initial state — the single-step "ship a rule" path that otherwise needs
`push rules-create` then `push rules-deploy`. The file must NOT already have a
companion .yaml (that rule is tracked — use rules-update / rules-deploy). The
companion .yaml is written next to the file on success. Multi-event rules that
cannot run LIVE fall back to HOURLY to preserve enabled=true. Guarded: dry-run
by default, --yes to apply.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alerting` | bool | true | initial deployment alerting state |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--enabled` | bool | true | initial deployment enabled state |
| `--run-frequency` | string | LIVE | initial run frequency: LIVE \| HOURLY \| DAILY |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

**Examples**

```bash
secopsctl rules promote detections/new-rule.yaral --dry-run
  secopsctl rules promote detections/new-rule.yaral --alerting=false --yes
```

## rules retrohunt create

MUTATING (guarded): start a retrohunt over the last --hours of data (rule accepts id, name, or slug)

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl rules retrohunt create <rule> [flags]
```

```text
Re-run a rule over the last --hours of already-stored data to surface
detections it would have produced. The retrohunt runs asynchronously —
poll its progress with `rules retrohunt get`/`rules retrohunt list`.
<rule> is a rule id, display name, or slug as shown by `rules list`.
Guarded: dry-run by default, --yes to apply against the live tenant.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--hours` | int | 168 | look-back window in hours (default 7d) |
| `--wait` | bool | false | poll until the retrohunt finishes, then report its final state |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## rules retrohunt get

Read-only: get one retrohunt's status (rule accepts id, name, or slug)

```text
secopsctl rules retrohunt get <rule> <retrohunt-id>
```

## rules retrohunt list

Read-only: list a rule's retrohunts (accepts id, display name, or slug)

```text
secopsctl rules retrohunt list <rule>
```

## rules review

Read-only: promotion report for monitor-mode rules (enabled, not alerting)

```text
secopsctl rules review [flags]
```

```text
Identify rules that are enabled but NOT alerting (monitor mode) and show
their detection activity over the last --hours. Rules with the most
detections appear first — the best promotion candidates. Use --min-detections
to filter out silent monitors.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--format` | string | - | output: table \| json \| csv (default table; overrides the global --output/--json) |
| `--hours` | int | 168 | detection-trend look-back window in hours (default 7d) |
| `--min-detections` | int | 0 | only show rules with at least N detections |
| `--out` | string | - | write to a file instead of stdout |

## rules test

Read-only: dry-run a YARA-L rule against historical data (streams detections, no deploy)

```text
secopsctl rules test <file.yaral> [flags]
```

```text
Run a YARA-L rule file over a window WITHOUT creating the rule, and report
the detections it would have produced (and any compile errors). Unlike
`rules validate` (compile-check only), this previews real matches — size a
rule's coverage and false-positive load before `rules promote`. Streams scan
progress and detections as they arrive; --no-stream buffers instead. The
window is the last --hours, or an explicit --from/--to. Read-only: nothing is
stored.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--from` | string | - | explicit start time (RFC3339 / ISO-8601); overrides --hours |
| `--hours` | int | 24 | look-back window in hours when --from is not given |
| `--max-results` | int | 100 | max detections to return (1-10000) |
| `--no-stream` | bool | false | buffer the whole result instead of streaming it |
| `--to` | string | - | explicit end time (RFC3339 / ISO-8601); default: now |

**Examples**

```bash
secopsctl rules test detections/new-rule.yaral --hours 24
  secopsctl rules test detections/new-rule.yaral --from 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z --to 2026-06-02T00:00:00Z --json
```

## rules trends

Read-only: per-rule detection counts + last detection — which rules are noisy or silent

```text
secopsctl rules trends [flags]
```

```text
Detection counts (bucketed by day over the window) and the last-detection
timestamp per rule, noisiest first — the data behind enable/alerting
decisions. No --rule = every rule on the instance. Curated rules have their
own `curated trends`.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--hours` | int | 168 | look-back window in hours (default 7 days) |
| `--rule` | string | - | comma-separated rule refs (id/name/slug); empty = all rules |

## rules validate

Validate a YARA-L file against the API (no mutation)

```text
secopsctl rules validate <file.yaral>
```

## rules versions

Read-only: list a rule's saved revisions; subcommands: diff, restore

```text
secopsctl rules versions <rule-id> [--show N] [flags]
```

```text
List a rule's revision history (newest first) — each save/deploy mints a
revision, identified by the @v_… suffix on its resource name. --show N prints
the YARA-L of the Nth listed revision. Compare two revisions with
`rules versions diff`, or roll back with the guarded `rules versions restore`.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--show` | int | 0 | print the Nth listed revision's YARA-L text instead of the list |

## rules versions diff

Read-only: line-by-line diff of two of a rule's revisions

```text
secopsctl rules versions diff <rule> <a> <b>
```

```text
Diff the YARA-L of two revisions of a rule. Each of <a>/<b> is either a
1-based index from `rules versions <rule>` or a v_… version token. <rule> is
an id, display name, or slug.
```

## rules versions restore

MUTATING (guarded): re-apply a prior revision's YARA-L as a new revision

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl rules versions restore <rule> <version> [flags]
```

```text
Roll a rule back to a prior revision by re-applying that revision's YARA-L —
this creates a NEW revision with the old text (it does not erase history).
<version> is a 1-based index from `rules versions <rule>` or a v_… token.
Guarded: dry-run by default (prints the diff), --yes to apply.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |
